PODPIS WĘŻA

Pod portretem Paradoksu

Nie przyszedłem pierwszy.
Nie odszedłem ostatni.

Zrzuciłem skórę,
lecz nie pamięć.

Widziałem światło,
które rzucało cień na siebie.

Widziałem ścianę,
która marzyła, żeby być drzwiami.

Nie powiedziałem prawdy.
Nie skłamałem.

Zostawiłem tylko ślad
tam, gdzie droga jeszcze nie istniała.

A kiedy zapytano, kim jestem,
odpowiedziałem:

— Tym samym. Już innym.

TRATADO TÉCNICO SOBRE CRIPTOGRAFÍA POST-CUÁNTICA, ARQUITECTURAS MULTICAPA, TOKENIZACIÓN DE RWA Y AUDITORÍA IA DE CONTRATOS INTELIGENTES
Estudio Integral de Fundamentos Físico-Matemáticos, Algoritmos de Ataque y Defensa, Escalabilidad Layer-2, Cumplimiento RegTech y Modelos de Lenguaje en Blockchain
Autoría / Rol: Arquitecto Senior de Sistemas Cuánticos y Criptografía Proyecto: Bloques Cuánticos Post-Cuánticos
Alcance: Análisis Exhaustivo Multidisciplinar (10 Dimensiones) Estado: Aprobado para Producción y Desarrollo

Tabla de Contenidos

(La Tabla de Contenidos se actualizará automáticamente al abrir el documento en Microsoft Word o Google Docs).
RESUMEN EJECUTIVO DE ARQUITECTURA
El presente tratado técnico ofrece una investigación rigurosa, profunda y matemáticamente fundamentada sobre la convergencia entre la física cuántica, la criptografía avanzada, las arquitecturas distribuibles de registros en cadena (blockchain), la tokenización de activos del mundo real (RWA), el cumplimiento normativo internacional y los modelos de lenguaje de gran escala (LLM) aplicados a la auditoría de contratos inteligentes. Basándose en la totalidad de la evidencia contenida en las diecinueve fuentes primarias del proyecto, este estudio establece la hoja de ruta para la construcción de infraestructuras financieras inmunes a amenazas cuánticas y con capacidad de procesamiento a escala masiva.
📌 SÍNTESIS ESTRATÉGICA GLOBAL
La tecnología blockchain se encuentra en una encrucijada crítica: mientras que los ordenadores cuánticos emergentes amenazan con romper la criptografía de clave pública tradicional (ECDSA/RSA) mediante el algoritmo de Shor, las demandas globales de rendimiento exigen soluciones de Capa 2 (Lightning, Spark, Stacks, Liquid, Ark) y la tokenización masiva de activos ($16 billones para 2030). La supervivencia del ecosistema depende de la integración armónica de Criptografía Post-Cuántica (PQC), Distribución de Claves Cuánticas (QKD), optimización algorítmica de Capa 1 (MTTBA) y automatización con IA (Corpus GiAnt).

SECCIÓN 1: FUNDAMENTOS FÍSICO-MATEMÁTICOS DE LA MECÁNICA CUÁNTICA Y SU IMPACTO EN LA INFORMACIÓN DISTRIBUIDA
La ciencia de la información cuántica moderna tiene sus raíces teóricas directas en los trabajos seminales publicados por John von Neumann entre 1927 y 1932. Von Neumann unificó los esquemas divergentes de la mecánica matricial de Heisenberg y la mecánica ondulatoria de Schrödinger bajo una estructura matemática rigurosa basada en la teoría de operadores en Espacios de Hilbert (H). Esta formulación no solo definió la física atómica del siglo XX, sino que sienta las bases para comprender los límites del cómputo y la criptografía contemporánea.
1.1 El Espacio de Hilbert, Superposición y Notación de Dirac
A diferencia de un bit clásico que solo puede tomar valores discretos b ∈ {0, 1}, un bit cuántico o qubit se representa como un vector de estado unitario en un espacio de Hilbert complejo de dos dimensiones H². En la notación de Dirac, el estado general de un qubit se escribe como:
|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, donde α, β ∈ ℂ y |α|² + |β|² = 1
Donde: α y β representan las amplitudes de probabilidad complejas. |α|² es la probabilidad de medir 0 y |β|² la de medir 1.

Geométricamente, el estado de un qubit puro se visualiza en la Esfera de Bloch, donde el vector de estado se parametriza mediante los ángulos polares θ y azimutal φ:
|ψ⟩ = cos(θ/2)|0⟩ + e^(iφ) sin(θ/2)|1⟩, θ ∈ [0, π], φ ∈ [0, 2π)
Donde: Representación continua sobre la superficie de una esfera unitaria tridimensional.

Cuando se extiende a un sistema de n qubits, la dimensión del espacio de Hilbert crece de forma exponencial como dim(H) = 2ⁿ. Debido al principio de superposición y al entrelazamiento cuántico, un ordenador cuántico puede procesar una combinación lineal de las 2ⁿ configuraciones posibles simultáneamente, otorgando una ventaja computacional masiva sobre los sistemas binarios clásicos.
1.2 Teoría de la Medición: De Medidas de von Neumann (PVM) a POVM
En la formulación original de von Neumann, una medición ideal sobre un observable representado por un operador autoadjunto (Hermítico) A = A† se describe mediante Medidas de Proyección Valuadas (PVM). Cada resultado posible aᵢ corresponde a un operador de proyección Pᵢ tal que Pᵢ Pⱼ = δᵢⱼ Pᵢ y ∑ Pᵢ = I. La probabilidad de obtener el resultado aᵢ sobre un estado dado por la matriz de densidad ρ es p(aᵢ) = Tr(Pᵢ ρ), y el estado post-medición colapsa instantáneamente a ρ' = (Pᵢ ρ Pᵢ) / Tr(Pᵢ ρ).
En la teoría de la información cuántica moderna (2025-2026), el marco de von Neumann se ha extendido hacia las Medidas de Valores de Operadores Positivos (POVM). Un POVM es un conjunto de operadores hermíticos positivos {Mₖ} que satisfacen Mₖ ≥ 0 y ∑ Mₖ = I. A diferencia de las PVMs, los operadores de un POVM no requieren ser ortogonales entre sí, lo que permite realizar tareas complejas como la discriminación inequívoca de estados no ortogonales y la optimización de protocolos criptográficos en sensores y detectores cuánticos.
1.3 Entropía de von Neumann y Entropías Unilaterales (One-Shot QIT)
Para cuantificar la incertidumbre y el contenido de información en ensambles cuánticos descritos por la matriz de densidad ρ, von Neumann introdujo la entropía cuántica:
S(ρ) = -Tr(ρ ln ρ) = -∑ λᵢ ln(λᵢ)
Donde: λᵢ son los autovalores de la matriz de densidad ρ. S(ρ) = 0 para estados puros y S(ρ) = ln(d) para estados máximamente mezclados.

En aplicaciones del mundo real sobre redes distorsionadas o de un solo uso (One-Shot Quantum Information Theory), la entropía asintótica de von Neumann es insuficiente. Se emplean familias de entropías de orden suave (Smooth Min- and Max-Entropies, H_min^ε, H_max^ε), derivadas de divergencias parentales (Relative Entropies), que definen los límites físicos exactos para la extracción de claves secretas en protocolos como QKD.
1.4 El Teorema del Doble Centralizador, Álgebras de von Neumann y el Corte de Heisenberg
Un pilar fundamental de la física matemática es el Teorema del Doble Centralizador de von Neumann, el cual establece que para una álgebra de operadores M que contiene la identidad sobre un espacio de Hilbert, su conmutante M' (el conjunto de todos los operadores que conmutan con cada elemento de M) satisface M'' = M. Este resultado clasifica las Álgebras de von Neumann en factores de Tipo I, Tipo II y Tipo III, proporcionando el marco matemático para campos cuánticos continuos, gravedad cuántica y criptografía en espacios de dimensión infinita.
Finalmente, von Neumann abordó la paradoja de la medición identificando la arbitrariedad del 'Corte de Heisenberg' (Heisenberg Cut): la frontera conceptual que separa el sistema observado (cuántico) del observador (clásico). Von Neumann demostró de manera célebre que la ubicación del corte es móvil y no altera las predicciones de medición probabilísticas para un único observador, un principio reevaluado en 2025 para resolver paradojas de observadores múltiples (como la paradoja del amigo de Wigner en cosmología y agujeros negros).
SECCIÓN 2: LA AMENAZA CUÁNTICA CRIPTOGRÁFICA: ANÁLISIS DE ALGORITMOS DE ATAQUE Y VULNERABILIDADES EN BLOCKCHAIN
La seguridad de las redes blockchain clásicas como Bitcoin, Ethereum y Monero descansa sobre dos pilares criptográficos: la criptografía de clave pública (utilizada para la generación de direcciones y firmas digitales de transacciones) y las funciones de hash criptográficas (utilizadas para el enlace inmutable de bloques, árboles de Merkle y mecanismos de consenso de Prueba de Trabajo). La llegada de ordenadores cuánticos universales destruye las garantías de seguridad de estos cimientos a través de dos algoritmos cuánticos específicos.
2.1 El Algoritmo de Shor y la Ruptura de la Criptografía Asimétrica (ECDSA / RSA)

items.title: The Shroud of Turin, Impressive Forgery or Garment of Christ? What are the implications if The Shroud is truly Jesus’ burial garment?
items.summary:
The Shroud of Turin, Impressive Forgery or Garment of Christ? What are the implications if The Shroud is truly Jesus’ burial garment?

In our post-modern Western society, we live in a world where science and religion are two separate domains that cannot coexist.
items.body_excerpt:
The Shroud of Turin, Impressive Forgery or Garment of Christ? What are the implications if The Shroud is truly Jesus’ burial garment?

In our post-modern Western society, we live in a world where science and religion are two separate domains that cannot coexist. However, society didn’t always think this way. Throughout history, people knew science and religion to be one in the same, working together and explaining one other’s existence. In many cultures, that lens is still used.. Today, we will put science and religion back into union with one another. To see if science can prove the Life, Death, and Resurrection of Jesus Christ.

Before investigating empirical evidence of who Jesus is, we first need to deal with some common questions and misconceptions about Jesus: Firstly,Is Jesus a real person? If so, what does Jesus say about himself? 

Some would argue that Jesus was never actually a real person at all and that his disciples just created a fictional being along with the entire New Testament. This doesn’t logically make sense, since even the Pharisees or Sadducees who despised Jesus at the time never accused him of being a fake person, and almost all major religions (such as Islam and Buddhism) accept Jesus to be, at the very least, a prophet or moral teacher. Nevertheless, we will still examine this claim using artifactual evidence and reasoning. One of the best pieces of evidence we have of Jesus’ existence is from Flavius Josephus’ record about Jewish history recorded in 93 AD in which Flavius said he, “Performed surprising deeds and was a teacher of such people as accept the truth gladly” (Jewish Antiquities 18.3.3). Josephus later goes on to reference that Jesus may even be the messiah himself, to which some question if he was really Jewish or if he was more Christian. While some could argue this account may be biased, it is a vital and early piece of evidence that validates Jesus’ existence. Perhaps an even more striking account comes from a man who hated Christians by the name of Publius Cornelius Tacitus. Tacitus says, “The founder of this name, Christ [Christus in Latin], had been executed in the reign of Tiberius by the procurator Pontius Pilate … Suppressed for a time, the deadly superstition erupted again not only in Judea, the origin of this evil, but also in the city [Rome], where all things horrible and shameful from everywhere come together and become popular”(Mykytiuk 2026, 1). While his authorial intent is to dissuade people from Christianity, he still gives the reader great insight into Jesus and general Christian truths. Firstly, he says that Jesus was executed by Pilate (26-36 CE) under emperor Tiberius (14-37 CE), which aligns with when New Testament scholars estimate Jesus to have died in 29 CE. On top of that “Happy Accident”, there is more revealed in Tacitus’ excerpt. Tacitus lists Judea as the origin of Christianity, which also parallels the Christian account that Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea. These corroborating sources imply that none of these similarities are coincidental. Even though Tacitus hated Christianity and referred to it as “evil” and “shameful” in his commentary, it still shows Jesus to be a real person, Lord or not.

Now that we have established historical evidence that Jesus is a real person (unlike Harry Potter), what did Jesus say about himself? Many individuals and religions like to assert that Jesus never actually claimed to be God in the Bible and that he was just a good teacher, or a prophet. However, in John chapter 8, a group of Jews questioned Jesus and accused him of demon possession when they asked him how he knew Abraham if he was not even 50 years old to which Jesus replies, “Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I am” (ESV John 8:58). What Jesus says here is in reference to Exodus 3:14 where God gives the Jewish people his personal name of Yahweh which means “I AM WHO I AM.” This statement speaks to God's person, being outside of time, space, and matter, which is a foundational piece for both the Jewish and Christian faith. Saying I am, means he always was and always will be. So when Jesus says this, he is claiming to be God and to have this characteristic of being the “Alpha and Omega”, and having his being before Abraham existed. Any Jew who understood the Torah at the time would have known exactly what Jesus was saying and furthermore, the Jews who were present, understood and attempted to stone him for blasphemy then and there. 

In addition to this excerpt, there is also a moment when Jesus is teaching the people and he says, “Whoever believes in me, believes not in me but in him who sent me… For I have not spoken on my own authority, but the Father who sent me has himself given me a commandment– what to say and what to speak. And I know that his commandment is eternal life” (ESV John 12:44-50). Jesus asserts multiple things here. Firstly, that he was sent by God directly, and that God gave him his commandment that is “eternal life”. Secondly, that Jesus and God the Father are one. As it says in verse 44, one who believes in Jesus believes in the one who sent him. Lastly, the Lord is Jesus’ father, which differentiates him from the prophets and gives a much more personal relationship with God and therefore one of higher importance. This clearly demonstrates that Jesus is claiming to be the Son of God and therefore has Authority on heaven and Earth, as God does. Therefore, Jesus may or may not have been God, but he very clearly and certainly claimed to be God multiple times throughout Scriptures. 

Now that we have cleared up some common misconceptions surrounding Jesus Christ, we will explore potential evidence that supports Jesus’ claim to be God. 

The Shroud of Turin: an impressive forgery or garment of Christ? The shroud of Turin is 14.3ft long by 3.7ft wide, and it displays a light brown/red stain which portrays a 5 '7 ft man’s frontal and dorsal sides (Britannica 2026, 1). However, if the man was really only 5 '7 ft tall, the question must be asked, why is the stain on the shroud visually longer than that? There are several key factors that explain this appearance. Firstly, the shroud was loose and oversized, so it would’ve draped over the contours of the body rather than being snug. Biology Insights science writer Daniel Beckett asks the reader to imagine they are being wrapped in a bed sheet when he says, “It would dip into the hollows behind the ankles, rise over the kneecaps, and sag between the chest and the pelvis. If you later laid that sheet flat and measured the distance along the image, the measurement would be longer than the person’s actual height” (Beckett, 2026). This clearly shows that due to the way the cloth was laid, whoever’s image appears on the shroud would appear larger just by looking at the blood stains. Another factor that may contribute to the different measurements in height is that if this was Jesus, then rigor mortis would have kept the body slightly stretched out from crucifixion, making it appear an inch or two longer due to the decompression of the spine. There are several other factors that would also affect the height analysis, like a slight bend in the knees and the man’s chin tilting down. With all of these considerations, it is nearly impossible to nail down an exact height based on the blood stain, but most experts estimate the man stood in a range of 5 '7 to 5’11ft. 

As well as these height considerations, there is also the question of if the shroud was just an impressive European renaissance art piece from the thirteenth or fourteenth century. Throughout various tests such as Energy Dispersive X-ray Analysis (EDX testing), protease testing, protein testing, identifying organic matrices, detecting bile pigments, and several other analyses, experts have determined that the stains on the shroud are in fact human blood. Furthermore, there is evidence of both pre-mortem and post-mortem blood on the shroud (Fanti 2024, 3). Thi

### Philosophically, intellectually—in every way—human society is unprepared for the rise of artificial intelligence.

Three years ago, at a conference on transatlantic issues, the subject of artificial intelligence appeared on the agenda.
items.body_excerpt:
The Atlantic

### Philosophically, intellectually—in every way—human society is unprepared for the rise of artificial intelligence.

Three years ago, at a conference on transatlantic issues, the subject of artificial intelligence appeared on the agenda. I was on the verge of skipping that session—it lay outside my usual concerns—but the beginning of the presentation held me in my seat.

The speaker described the workings of a computer program that would soon challenge international champions in the game Go. I was amazed that a computer could master Go, which is more complex than chess. In it, each player deploys 180 or 181 pieces (depending on which color he or she chooses), placed alternately on an initially empty board; victory goes to the side that, by making better strategic decisions, immobilizes his or her opponent by more effectively controlling territory.

The speaker insisted that this ability could not be preprogrammed. His machine, he said, learned to master Go by training itself through practice. Given Go’s basic rules, the computer played innumerable games against itself, learning from its mistakes and refining its algorithms accordingly. In the process, it exceeded the skills of its human mentors. And indeed, in the months following the speech, an AI program named AlphaGo would decisively defeat the world’s greatest Go players.

As I listened to the speaker celebrate this technical progress, my experience as a historian and occasional practicing statesman gave me pause. What would be the impact on history of self-learning machines—machines that acquired knowledge by processes particular to themselves, and applied that knowledge to ends for which there may be no category of human understanding? Would these machines learn to communicate with one another? How would choices be made among emerging options? Was it possible that human history might go the way of the Incas, faced with a Spanish culture incomprehensible and even awe-inspiring to them? Were we at the edge of a new phase of human history?

Aware of my lack of technical competence in this field, I organized a number of informal dialogues on the subject, with the advice and cooperation of acquaintances in technology and the humanities. These discussions have caused my concerns to grow.

Heretofore, the technological advance that most altered the course of modern history was the invention of the printing press in the 15th century, which allowed the search for empirical knowledge to supplant liturgical doctrine, and the Age of Reason to gradually supersede the Age of Religion. Individual insight and scientific knowledge replaced faith as the principal criterion of human consciousness. Information was stored and systematized in expanding libraries. The Age of Reason originated the thoughts and actions that shaped the contemporary world order.

But that order is now in upheaval amid a new, even more sweeping technological revolution whose consequences we have failed to fully reckon with, and whose culmination may be a world relying on machines powered by data and algorithms and ungoverned by ethical or philosophical norms.

The internet age in which we already live prefigures some of the questions and issues that AI will only make more acute. The Enlightenment sought to submit traditional verities to a liberated, analytic human reason. The internet’s purpose is to ratify knowledge through the accumulation and manipulation of ever expanding data. Human cognition loses its personal character. Individuals turn into data, and data become regnant.

Users of the internet emphasize retrieving and manipulating information over contextualizing or conceptualizing its meaning. They rarely interrogate history or philosophy; as a rule, they demand information relevant to their immediate practical needs. In the process, search-engine algorithms acquire the capacity to predict the preferences of individual clients, enabling the algorithms to personalize results and make them available to other parties for political or commercial purposes. Truth becomes relative. Information threatens to overwhelm wisdom.

Inundated via social media with the opinions of multitudes, users are diverted from introspection; in truth many technophiles use the internet to avoid the solitude they dread. All of these pressures weaken the fortitude required to develop and sustain convictions that can be implemented only by traveling a lonely road, which is the essence of creativity.

The impact of internet technology on politics is particularly pronounced. The ability to target micro-groups has broken up the previous consensus on priorities by permitting a focus on specialized purposes or grievances. Political leaders, overwhelmed by niche pressures, are deprived of time to think or reflect on context, contracting the space available for them to develop vision.

The digital world’s emphasis on speed inhibits reflection; its incentive empowers the radical over the thoughtful; its values are shaped by subgroup consensus, not by introspection. For all its achievements, it runs the risk of turning on itself as its impositions overwhelm its conveniences.

As the internet and increased computing power have facilitated the accumulation and analysis of vast data, unprecedented vistas for human understanding have emerged. Perhaps most significant is the project of producing artificial intelligence—a technology capable of inventing and solving complex, seemingly abstract problems by processes that seem to replicate those of the human mind.

This goes far beyond automation as we have known it. Automation deals with means; it achieves prescribed objectives by rationalizing or mechanizing instruments for reaching them. AI, by contrast, deals with ends; it establishes its own objectives. To the extent that its achievements are in part shaped by itself, AI is inherently unstable. AI systems, through their very operations, are in constant flux as they acquire and instantly analyze new data, then seek to improve themselves on the basis of that analysis. Through this process, artificial intelligence develops an ability previously thought to be reserved for human beings. It makes strategic judgments about the future, some based on data received as code (for example, the rules of a game), and some based on data it gathers itself (for example, by playing 1 million iterations of a game).

The driverless car illustrates the difference between the actions of traditional human-controlled, software-powered computers and the universe AI seeks to navigate. Driving a car requires judgments in multiple situations impossible to anticipate and hence to program in advance. What would happen, to use a well-known hypothetical example, if such a car were obliged by circumstance to choose between killing a grandparent and killing a child? Whom would it choose? Why? Which factors among its options would it attempt to optimize? And could it explain its rationale? Challenged, its truthful answer would likely be, were it able to communicate: “I don’t know (because I am following mathematical, not human, principles),” or “You would not understand (because I have been trained to act in a certain way but not to explain it).” Yet driverless cars are likely to be prevalent on roads within a decade.

We must expect AI to make mistakes faster—and of greater magnitude—than humans do.

Heretofore confined to specific fields of activity, AI research now seeks to bring about a “generally intelligent” AI capable of executing tasks in multiple fields. A growing percentage of human activity will, within a measurable time period, be driven by AI algorithms. But these algorithms, being mathematical interpretations of observed data, do not explain the underlying reality that produces them. Paradoxically, as the world becomes more transparent, it will also become increasingly mysterious. What will distinguish that new world from the one we have known? How will we live in it? How will

items.body_excerpt:
![OnALegendsArticle](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/starwars/images/d/d6/OnALegendsArticle.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/150?cb=20250314035545)

OnALegendsArticle

**Olag Greck** was a businessman and later a [crime lord](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Crime_lord/Legends "Crime lord/Legends") who lived during the [Imperial Era](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Imperial_Era/Legends "Imperial Era/Legends").

## Biography

Greck was a partner of [Baron](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Baron/Legends "Baron/Legends") [Pitareeze](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Pitareeze "Pitareeze"), when the Baron was trying to get his shipbuilding business off the ground. He betrayed the Baron, stealing his plans for the [Pitareeze Cruiser](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Pitareeze_Cruiser "Pitareeze Cruiser") while the Baron slept, and produced cheaper versions of it. He sold these claiming that they were his own original designs. When key components of Greck's ships failed, however, he begged for the Baron's help in fixing the flaws, but Pitareeze refused. Olag Greck then kidnapped the Baron's grandson, [Nak Pitareeze](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Nak_Pitareeze "Nak Pitareeze") and forced him to fix his ships. Greck's plan was foiled before the ships were fixed. [C-3PO](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/C-3PO/Legends "C-3PO/Legends") and [R2-D2](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/R2-D2/Legends "R2-D2/Legends"), who had come into the possession of the Pitareeze, helped stop several of his schemes. An angered Greck blamed the ship's failure on the Baron's intervention.

Greck ran a series of illegal operations on or around [Hosk Station](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Hosk_Station/Legends "Hosk Station/Legends"). One such operation was the [droid](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Droid/Legends "Droid/Legends") arena, where combat droids were pitted against one another. Earlier, he had foolishly had [IG-88B](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/IG-88B/Legends "IG-88B/Legends") brought to the station to fight in the arena. IG-88B humiliated Greck, stealing a ship and escaping from Hosk. Greck also reprogrammed [C-3PX](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/C-3PX "C-3PX") to work for him, though the droid was ultimately defeated by R2-D2.

He was finally caught on Hosk, attempting to steal a load of ash ore. He planned to destroy the station to cover his escape. Unit [Zed](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Zed "Zed"), along with C-3PO, R2-D2, and several other droids managed to prevent the detonation, but Greck still escaped. Unit Zed, C-3PO, and R2-D2 followed him to [Nar Shaddaa](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Nar_Shaddaa/Legends "Nar Shaddaa/Legends"), where he was going to meet with his acquaintance, [Movo Brattakin](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Movo_Brattakin "Movo Brattakin"). Damaged by Zed, Greck's ship crashed into the hangar where Brattakin was waiting, fatally injuring him. Brattakin's head of security and Greck's former associate [Jace Forno](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Jace_Forno "Jace Forno") threw Greck in jail for killing Brattakin. Grek escaped and went to [Boonda's](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Boonda/Legends "Boonda/Legends") Palace to make a deal with the [Hutt](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Hutt/Legends "Hutt/Legends"). It was here that C-3PO and R2-D2 caught up with him again, though little did they know that all that was transpiring was part of Movo Brattakin's plan. Brattakin's faithful droid, [B-9D7](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/B-9D7 "B-9D7"), had extracted his master's brain from his dying body and transplanted it into his own cranium. He appeared at the palace, threatening to destroy it if anyone moved. It was then that Jace Forno arrived, and unfortunately for Brattakin, Forno betrayed him, decapitating his droid body with a [blaster](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Blaster/Legends "Blaster/Legends") bolt. Greck tried to continue with his business with Boonda, but instead became Boonda's captive. Greck later escaped, and went underground for several years.

Olag Greck turned up again on [Corellia](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Corellia/Legends "Corellia/Legends"), where he earned a reputation as a disreputable businessbeing. He became the leader of the [Greck](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Greck "Greck"), that was a gang that consisted of thugs hired by him.[^2]

## Behind the scenes

![Unused model of Olag Greck for Star Wars Galaxies, depicted as an ](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/starwars/images/c/c9/Olag_Greck_SWG.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/200?cb=20221203095646)

Unused model of Olag Greck for Star Wars Galaxies, depicted as an Ishi Tib

Olag Greck was mentioned in the [2003](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/2003 "2003") [video game](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars_video_games "Star Wars video games") *[Star Wars Galaxies](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars_Galaxies "Star Wars Galaxies")*, a [massively multiplayer online roleplaying game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massively_multiplayer_online_role-playing_game "wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game") developed by [Sony](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Sony "Sony") Online Entertainment and published by [LucasArts](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/LucasArts "LucasArts"),[^1] prior to its closure on [December 15](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/December_15 "December 15"), [2011](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/2011 "2011").[^3] In the game, he was the leader of the eponymous faction but did not appear himself.[^1] Unused game files revealed that the developers planed at some point to introduce Olag Greck as a [non-player character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-player_character "wikipedia:Non-player character") in *Star Wars Galaxies*.[^4] According to these files, introduced with the " [Publish 28](https://swg.fandom.com/wiki/Publish_28_Notes_for_April_26,_2006 "w:c:swg:Publish 28 Notes for April 26, 2006")," on [April 26](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/April_26 "April 26"), [2006](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/2006 "2006"),[^5] Olag Greck would have been present on Corellia and involved in a questline named "Tyrena - Lyman Zavala." In this quests, the player would have been tasked by [CorSec](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Corellian_Security_Force "Corellian Security Force") [Captain](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Captain/Legends "Captain/Legends") [Dool](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Dool "Dool") and the [Tyrena](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Tyrena/Legends "Tyrena/Legends") city councilmen [Lyman Zavala](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Lyman_Zavala "Lyman Zavala") to investigate the relationship between the [Chirq Council](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Chirq_Council "Chirq Council") and the Greck criminals. Olag Greck was intended to be the final boss to kill to conclude the questline. However, Greck is not known to have appeared on the game's live servers. Nevertheless, an emulated depiction pulled from this character's Interchange File Format reveals what he would have looked like if he were added to the game.[^1]

items.body_excerpt:
![https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Truvada.JPG/250px-Truvada.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Truvada.JPG/250px-Truvada.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail "SHA-256: 92c6fab93c9dddde4d1623d0417e453148cec5bd6a6d68537ff2f1478cca3d7f")

Tablets of Truvada, an emtricitabine/tenofovir combination used for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis

**Pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV prevention**, commonly known as **PrEP** (pronounced as *prep*, [/ p r ɛ p /](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English")), is the use of [antiviral drugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antiviral_drugs "Antiviral drugs") as a strategy for the [prevention of HIV/AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prevention_of_HIV/AIDS "Prevention of HIV/AIDS") by people that do not have HIV/AIDS.[^1] PrEP is one of a number of [HIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV "HIV") prevention strategies for people who are HIV-negative but who have a higher risk of acquiring HIV, including sexually active adults who are at increased risk of contracting HIV, people who engage in intravenous drug use (see [drug injection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_injection "Drug injection")), and [serodiscordant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serodiscordant "Serodiscordant") sexually active couples.[^2]

The first form of PrEP for HIV prevention— [emtricitabine and tenofovir disoproxil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emtricitabine/tenofovir "Emtricitabine/tenofovir") (FTC/TDF; Truvada)—was approved in 2012.[^3] In October 2019, the US [Food and Drug Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_and_Drug_Administration "Food and Drug Administration") (FDA) approved the combination of [emtricitabine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emtricitabine "Emtricitabine") and [tenofovir alafenamide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenofovir_alafenamide "Tenofovir alafenamide") (FTC/TAF; Descovy) to be used as PrEP in addition to Truvada, which provides similar levels of protection.[^4] Descovy, however, is currently approved only for [cisgender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisgender "Cisgender") men and [transgender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") women as the efficacy has not been assessed in people at risk for HIV through [receptive vaginal sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penile-vaginal_intercourse "Penile-vaginal intercourse").[^2]

In December 2021, the US FDA approved [cabotegravir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabotegravir "Cabotegravir") (Apretude), which is an injectable form of PrEP manufactured by [Viiv Healthcare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viiv_Healthcare "Viiv Healthcare"). Regulators believe it will improve medication adherence because it has to be taken just once every two months, and it will also widen adoption as it eliminates the need to hide pills or pharmacy visits for discretion.[^5]

In its 2021 guidelines, the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") (WHO) recommends several options for PrEP, tailored to different populations and circumstances:[^6]

- Oral PrEP using TDF-containing compounds for anyone at substantial risk of HIV infection;
- Event-driven PrEP for [men who have sex with men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men_who_have_sex_with_men "Men who have sex with men") (MSM); and
- The [dapivirine vaginal ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dapivirine_Ring "Dapivirine Ring") (DPV-VR) for women at substantial risk of HIV infection who do not have access to oral PrEP.[^6]

On 18 June 2025, the [FDA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_and_Drug_Administration "Food and Drug Administration") approved the long-acting HIV prevention antiretroviral [lenacapavir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenacapavir "Lenacapavir") in the United States.[^7] The drug is branded as Yeztugo by [Gilead Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilead_Sciences "Gilead Sciences") and requires only two [subcutaneous injections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subcutaneous_injections "Subcutaneous injections") per year, demonstrating high efficacy in clinical trials by offering nearly complete protection against [HIV infection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV_infection "HIV infection").[^8] As the second PrEP extended-release option following [cabotegravir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabotegravir "Cabotegravir"), lenacapavir's simplified dosing schedule could significantly improve patient access and adherence, especially for populations at higher risk of HIV.[^9] However, the global rollout may be challenged by recent funding reductions by the Trump Administration in [global health funding by the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_health_funding_by_the_United_States "Global health funding by the United States") that were expected to support lenacapavir access in lower-income countries across sub-Saharan Africa by [PEPFAR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President's_Emergency_Plan_for_AIDS_Relief "President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief").[^10] In September 2025, global partnerships set lenacapavir's HIV prevention price at US$40 per patient annually in 120 low- and middle-income countries.[^11] The [WHO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") is planning to adopt [lenacapavir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenacapavir "Lenacapavir") in global guidelines for resource-limited settings as well as for WHO pre-qualification regulatory approval.[^12]

## Medical uses

### Indications for use

#### United States

In the United States, federal guidelines updated in 2021 now recommend healthcare providers discuss and provide information on the use of PrEP for HIV prevention for all sexually active adults and adolescents.[^2] The US [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Disease_Control_and_Prevention "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention") (CDC) recommends providers take a targeted sexual history of their patients to assess specific risk for HIV acquisition and suggest PrEP to the following patients:[^2]

- Sexually active adults and adolescents who have had anal or vaginal sex in the past six months and any of the following:
 - One or more partner(s) with unknown HIV status and inconsistent condom use;
 - An HIV-positive sexual partner (especially if they have an unknown or detectable viral load);
 - A bacterial [sexually transmitted infection (STI)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexually_transmitted_infection "Sexually transmitted infection") in the past six months.
- Patients reporting injection drug use within the last six months and any of the following:
 - An HIV-positive injecting partner;
 - Shared injection equipment.

Additionally, these updated guidelines recommend providers prescribe PrEP to any patient that requests it, regardless of their stated risk factors.[^2]

#### United Kingdom

In the United Kingdom the *BHIVA/BASHH guidelines on the use of HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) 2018* [^13] recommend:

- On-demand or daily oral [tenofovir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenofovir "Tenofovir") – [emtricitabine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emtricitabine "Emtricitabine") (TD-FTC) for HIV-negative MSM who are at elevated risk of HIV acquisition through unprotected anal sex in the previous six months and ongoing unprotected anal sex.
- On-demand or daily oral TD-FTC for HIV-negative MSM having unprotected anal sex with partners who are HIV-positive, unless the partner has been on AntiRetroviral Therapy (ART) for at least six months and their plasma viral load is <200 copies/mL.
- Tenofovir (TDF) alone should not be offered to MSM.

items.summary: **Alprazolam**, sold under the brand name **Xanax** among others, is a fast-acting, potent [tranquilizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranquilizer "Tranquilizer") of moderate duration within the [triazolobenzodiazepine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triazolobenzodiazepine "Tria…
items.body_excerpt:
**Alprazolam**, sold under the brand name **Xanax** among others, is a fast-acting, potent [tranquilizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tranquilizer "Tranquilizer") of moderate duration within the [triazolobenzodiazepine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triazolobenzodiazepine "Triazolobenzodiazepine") group of chemicals called [benzodiazepines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzodiazepine "Benzodiazepine").[^15] Alprazolam is most commonly prescribed in the management of [anxiety disorders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety_disorder "Anxiety disorder"), especially [panic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_disorder "Panic disorder") and [generalized anxiety disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_anxiety_disorder "Generalized anxiety disorder") (GAD).[^8] Other uses include the treatment of [chemotherapy-induced nausea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemotherapy-induced_nausea_and_vomiting "Chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting"), together with other treatments.[^14] Alprazolam is generally taken [orally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_administration "Oral administration").[^14]

Common side effects include [sleepiness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleepiness "Sleepiness"), [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depression_\(mood\) "Depression (mood)"), [suppressed emotions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reduced_affect_display "Reduced affect display"), mild to severe [decreases in motor skills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ataxia "Ataxia"), [hiccups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiccup "Hiccup"), dulling or declining of [cognition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cognition "Cognition"), decreased [alertness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alertness "Alertness"), [dry mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xerostomia "Xerostomia") (mildly), [decreased heart rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradycardia "Bradycardia"), impairment of judgment (usually in higher than therapeutic doses), and [decreased memory formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterograde_amnesia "Anterograde amnesia"),[^16] depending on dosage.[^14] Some of the sedation and drowsiness may improve within a few days.[^17]

[Benzodiazepine withdrawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benzodiazepine_withdrawal_syndrome "Benzodiazepine withdrawal syndrome") symptoms may occur if use is suddenly decreased.[^14] [^18]

Alprazolam was developed by Jackson Hester Jr. at the [Upjohn Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upjohn "Upjohn") [^19] and patented in 1971 and approved for medical use in the United States in 1981.[^14] [^20] Alprazolam is a [Schedule IV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Controlled_Substances_Act#Schedule_IV_controlled_substances "Controlled Substances Act") controlled substance and is a common drug of abuse.[^3] [^21] It is available as a [generic medication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generic_medication "Generic medication").[^8] In 2023, it was the 37th most commonly prescribed medication in the United States, with more than 15 million prescriptions.[^22] [^23]

## Medical uses

![https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Boites_d'alprazolam444.jpg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Boites_d'alprazolam444.jpg "SHA-256: 17b74bbc6248bd987d15f5e9835061327977a2429ffa4484642ce273ca12a821")

Alprazolam pills in boxes, as sold in France; both the original Pfizer brand product Xanax and various generic forms of alprazolam are depicted here.

![https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Xanax_2_mg.jpg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Xanax_2_mg.jpg "SHA-256: 27a2edf14e1dfaa09c0f22ee54b680c575b703a19aa477c23d15a61913d33397")

A prescription bottle of Xanax

![https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alprazolam_Tablets_China.jpg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alprazolam_Tablets_China.jpg "SHA-256: edcc6f636a2eeaeca19111d5c0a8b6275cbadcff7e01db787a565d3e86aaf13f")

Alprazolam tablets sold in China

Alprazolam is used in the management of [anxiety disorders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety_disorder "Anxiety disorder") and [nausea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nausea "Nausea") due to [chemotherapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemotherapy "Chemotherapy").[^14] Alprazolam is [indicated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indication_\(medicine\) "Indication (medicine)") for the treatment of [generalized anxiety disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generalized_anxiety_disorder "Generalized anxiety disorder") (GAD) and [panic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_disorder "Panic disorder") with or without [agoraphobia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agoraphobia "Agoraphobia") in adults.[^8]

### Panic disorder

Alprazolam is effective in the relief of moderate to severe [anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety "Anxiety") and [panic attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_attack "Panic attack").[^8] In [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"), alprazolam is not recommended for the treatment of [panic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_disorder "Panic disorder") because of concerns regarding [tolerance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_tolerance "Drug tolerance"), [dependence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substance_dependence "Substance dependence"), and [abuse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substance_abuse "Substance abuse").[^24] Most evidence shows that the benefits of alprazolam in treating panic disorder last only four to ten weeks. However, people with panic disorder have been treated on an open basis for up to eight months without apparent loss of benefit.[^8]

Alprazolam is recommended by the World Federation of Societies of Biological Psychiatry (WFSBP) for treatment-resistant cases of panic disorder where there is no history of tolerance or dependence.[^25]

A 2023 [meta-analysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meta-analysis "Meta-analysis") of published and unpublished FDA-submitted regulatory trials of alprazolam extended-release for panic disorder found that only one of five clinical trials showed a positive efficacy outcome (20%), while the rest were negative and did not demonstrate effectiveness.[^26] In the published literature, three trials were published conveying a positive outcome (100%), but of these, only one was positive and the other two were considered to have been inappropriately spun as positive.[^26] The [effect size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Effect_size "Effect size") ([Hedges's g](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedges's_g "Hedges's g")) of alprazolam extended-release for the treatment of panic disorder based on the five clinical trials was 0.33 (a small effect) and based on the published trials was 0.47 (a moderate effect), equating to an increase of 0.14 or 42%.[^26] The authors concluded that [publication bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Publication_bias "Publication bias") substantially inflated the effectiveness of alprazolam extended-release for panic disorder.[^26]

### Anxiety disorders

[Anxiety](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety "Anxiety") associated with [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_depressive_disorder "Major depressive disorder") is responsive to alprazolam. Clinical studies have shown that the effectiveness is limited to four months for [anxiety disorders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anxiety_disorder "Anxiety disorder").[^8] However, the research into [antidepressant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antidepressant "Antidepressant") properties of alprazolam is poor and has only assessed its short-term effects against depression.[^27] In one study, some long term, high-dosage users of alprazolam developed reversible depression.[^28]

# Chip Robot 0: chain-derived series rules

This is a new application protocol, not Bitcoin consensus or native UCO.
Deployment is an Ordinals envelope tagged `chiprobot/0`. This document is
embedded verbatim in the deployment body. No issuer signature, API, clock,
database, external randomness service or discretionary delivery is authoritative.
Each series activates only after its own definition is confirmed as specified below.

## Definition and identity

The series identifier is the definition inscription ID (64 lowercase display
hex txid, `i`, canonical decimal envelope index). Envelope enumeration and
parsing follow UCO v0.1 section 3 at upstream commit
19260366f1807109cfa3c40e35ce3b79eaaf268e. These parsing rules do not imply
that the resulting object is a UCO Module or Machine.
The envelope must have no duplicate/incomplete/unknown-even fields, content
encoding or delegate, must have content type application/json, and no metadata.
The body is UTF-8 canonical JSON: keys sorted, no insignificant whitespace,
ASCII escaped as Python ensure_ascii=True, no duplicate keys. Maximum 131072 bytes.

Required and only keys: protocol, version, genesisHash, policy, rules,
rulesSha256, netlistHex, rendererSvg. protocol is chiprobot/0, version is integer 0.
genesisHash binds the Bitcoin network. rules equals these exact UTF-8 bytes;
rulesSha256 is their SHA256. The static SVG is part of this immutable body,
not executable code. Rendering is nonconsensus: do not execute inscription HTML.

policy is exactly: supply 21000, perAddress 1, perBlock 1, drawOffset 6,
drawConfirmations 6, initialState 7, minOutputSats 330,
colors [[silver,6000],[green,2500],[blue,1000],[purple,400],[gold,100]].
All numeric values are integers. netlistHex is the lowercase TAP-02 encoding
of the 2-input, 8-output, 8-LATCH circuit described below; it must satisfy the
complete 1024-case behavior/output table, not just a claimed content hash.
Any well-formed NAND/LATCH-only implementation of that table is accepted.
No REF is accepted. Maximum 4096 records. Signatures/fees are not circuit inputs.

The series becomes eligible in the block AFTER its definition confirms.
Copying its contents creates a different series ID. There is no reserved
issuer allocation, bypass key, upgrade action or separate test allocation.

## Records and authentication

Only Bitcoin consensus-valid, canonical confirmed transactions count.
Mempool transactions never count. Coinbase never contains a valid record.
An indexer must use a validating node, not accept caller-supplied authentication.
Outpoint/prevout values and scripts must come from validated chain data.
Missing chain data is a fatal incomplete-index error, never an invalid-user verdict.

A carrier is OP_RETURN followed by exactly one data push starting with ASCII
CRB (hex 435242). Nonminimal push encodings are accepted. A transaction with
anything other than exactly one such carrier has no valid record. Other
OP_RETURN outputs do not count as carriers. Unknown kinds, trailing bytes and
truncated records have no valid record.

Payload = CRB || kind:u8 || definitionTxid:32 || envelopeIndex:u32be || tail.
Definition txid bytes use displayed big-endian order, NOT Bitcoin internal order.
Kinds: 1 ENTRY (empty tail), 2 STEP (action:u8,newState:u8), 3 MOVE (empty tail).
No record supplies a serial number, color, claimed owner or winner.

ENTRY: input 0 spends a P2TR output and uses exactly one witness element: either
a 64-byte SIGHASH_DEFAULT signature or a 65-byte signature ending in 01
(SIGHASH_ALL). Annex, script-path and other sighash modes are excluded in v0.
Bitcoin consensus verifies that signature, committing to the entry and outputs.
Output 0 must be P2TR, at least 330 sats, and have the identical scriptPubKey
as input 0's prevout. This proves control of the recipient output key on chain.
Identity is the complete scriptPubKey, not an address string. The candidate
pet outpoint is ENTRY txid:0. Other outputs are change/fees, never candidates.
No input may spend a pending candidate or live pet of THIS series. ENTRY may
use other ordinary inputs. Cross-series asset protection is a wallet duty.

## Per-block lottery

Round H comprises all valid ENTRY transactions confirmed at height H in this
series. Keep the FIRST valid transaction per recipient script in Bitcoin block
transaction order; duplicate attempts have no extra ticket. An entry, once
accepted, cannot be canceled or moved to another round by later spending it.

At the END of H+6, after processing that block's transactions, evaluate round H.
Remove addresses selected as winners in earlier rounds, including destroyed
winners. Sort remaining entries by lowercase display TXID ascending.
If no entries remain, or 21000 awards already exist, there is no winner.
Otherwise exactly one entry is selected; no redraw on lost, spent or frozen output.
Award serials start at 1 and increment by round height. Missed/empty rounds
do not consume supply.

Autoría / Rol: Arquitecto Senior de Sistemas Cuánticos y Criptografía Proyecto: Bloques Cuánticos Post-Cuánticos
Alcance: Análisis Exhaustivo Multidisciplinar (10 Dimensiones) Estado: Aprobado para Producción y Desarrollo

RESUMEN EJECUTIVO DE ARQUITECTURA
El presente tratado técnico ofrece una investigación rigurosa, profunda y matemáticamente fundamentada sobre la convergencia entre la física cuántica, la criptografía avanzada, las arquitecturas distribuibles de registros en cadena (blockchain), la tokenización de activos del mundo real (RWA), el cumplimiento normativo internacional y los modelos de lenguaje de gran escala (LLM) aplicados a la auditoría de contratos inteligentes. Basándose en la totalidad de la evidencia contenida en las diecinueve fuentes primarias del proyecto, este estudio establece la hoja de ruta para la construcción de infraestructuras financieras inmunes a amenazas cuánticas y con capacidad de procesamiento a escala masiva.
📌 SÍNTESIS ESTRATÉGICA GLOBAL
La tecnología blockchain se encuentra en una encrucijada crítica: mientras que los ordenadores cuánticos emergentes amenazan con romper la criptografía de clave pública tradicional (ECDSA/RSA) mediante el algoritmo de Shor, las demandas globales de rendimiento exigen soluciones de Capa 2 (Lightning, Spark, Stacks, Liquid, Ark) y la tokenización masiva de activos ($16 billones para 2030). La supervivencia del ecosistema depende de la integración armónica de Criptografía Post-Cuántica (PQC), Distribución de Claves Cuánticas (QKD), optimización algorítmica de Capa 1 (MTTBA) y automatización con IA (Corpus GiAnt).

SECCIÓN 1: FUNDAMENTOS FÍSICO-MATEMÁTICOS DE LA MECÁNICA CUÁNTICA Y SU IMPACTO EN LA INFORMACIÓN DISTRIBUIDA
La ciencia de la información cuántica moderna tiene sus raíces teóricas directas en los trabajos seminales publicados por John von Neumann entre 1927 y 1932. Von Neumann unificó los esquemas divergentes de la mecánica matricial de Heisenberg y la mecánica ondulatoria de Schrödinger bajo una estructura matemática rigurosa basada en la teoría de operadores en **Espacios de Hilbert** (\(\mathcal{H}\)). Esta formulación no solo definió la física atómica del siglo XX, sino que sienta las bases para comprender los límites del cómputo y la criptografía contemporánea.
1.1 El Espacio de Hilbert, Superposición y Notación de Dirac
A diferencia de un bit clásico que solo puede tomar valores discretos \(b \in \{0, 1\}\), un bit cuántico o **qubit** se representa como un vector de estado unitario en un espacio de Hilbert complejo de dos dimensiones \(\mathcal{H}^2\). En la notación de Dirac, el estado general de un qubit se escribe como:
|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, donde α, β ∈ ℂ y |α|² + |β|² = 1
Donde: α y β representan las amplitudes de probabilidad complejas. |α|² es la probabilidad de medir 0 y |β|² la de medir 1.

Geométricamente, el estado de un qubit puro se visualiza en la **Esfera de Bloch**, donde el vector de estado se parametriza mediante los ángulos polares \(\theta\) y azimutal \(\phi\):
|ψ⟩ = cos(θ/2)|0⟩ + e^(iφ) sin(θ/2)|1⟩, θ ∈ [0, π], φ ∈ [0, 2π)
Donde: Representación continua sobre la superficie de una esfera unitaria tridimensional.

Cuando se extiende a un sistema de \(n\) qubits, la dimensión del espacio de Hilbert crece de forma exponencial como \(\dim(\mathcal{H}) = 2^n\). Debido al principio de **superposición** y al **entrelazamiento cuántico**, un ordenador cuántico puede procesar una combinación lineal de las \(2^n\) configuraciones posibles simultáneamente, otorgando una ventaja computacional masiva sobre los sistemas binarios clásicos.
1.2 Teoría de la Medición: De Medidas de von Neumann (PVM) a POVM
En la formulación original de von Neumann, una medición ideal sobre un observable representado por un operador autoadjunto (Hermítico) \(A = A^\dagger\) se describe mediante **Medidas de Proyección Valuadas (PVM)**. Cada resultado posible \(a_i\) corresponde a un operador de proyección \(P_i\) tal que \(P_i P_j = \delta_{ij} P_i\) y \(\sum_i P_i = I\). La probabilidad de obtener el resultado \(a_i\) sobre un estado dado por la matriz de densidad \(\rho\) es \(p(a_i) = \text{Tr}(P_i \rho)\), y el estado post-medición colapsa instantáneamente a \(\rho' = \frac{P_i \rho P_i}{\text{Tr}(P_i \rho)}\).
En la teoría de la información cuántica moderna (2025-2026), el marco de von Neumann se ha extendido hacia las **Medidas de Valores de Operadores Positivos (POVM)**. Un POVM es un conjunto de operadores hermíticos positivos \(\{M_k\}\) que satisfacen \(M_k \geq 0\) y \(\sum_k M_k = I\). A diferencia de las PVMs, los operadores de un POVM no requieren ser ortogonales entre sí, lo que permite realizar tareas complejas como la discriminación inequívoca de estados no ortogonales y la optimización de protocolos criptográficos en sensores y detectores cuánticos.
1.3 Entropía de von Neumann y Entropías Unilaterales (One-Shot QIT)
Para cuantificar la incertidumbre y el contenido de información en ensambles cuánticos descritos por la matriz de densidad \(\rho\), von Neumann introdujo la entropía cuántica:
S(ρ) = -Tr(ρ ln ρ) = -∑ λ_i ln(λ_i)
Donde: donde λ_i son los autovalores de la matriz de densidad ρ. S(ρ) = 0 para estados puros y S(ρ) = ln(d) para estados máximamente mezclados.

En aplicaciones del mundo real sobre redes distorsionadas o de un solo uso (One-Shot Quantum Information Theory), la entropía asintótica de von Neumann es insuficiente. Se emplean familias de entropías de orden suave (Smooth Min- and Max-Entropies, \(H_{\min}^\epsilon, H_{\max}^\epsilon\)), derivadas de divergencias parentales (Relative Entropies), que definen los límites físicos exactos para la extracción de claves secretas en protocolos como QKD.
1.4 El Teorema del Doble Centralizador, Álgebras de von Neumann y el Corte de Heisenberg
Un pilar fundamental de la física matemática es el **Teorema del Doble Centralizador de von Neumann**, el cual establece que para una álgebra de operadores \(\mathcal{M}\) que contiene la identidad sobre un espacio de Hilbert, su conmutante \(\mathcal{M}'\) (el conjunto de todos los operadores que conmutan con cada elemento de \(\mathcal{M}\)) satisface \(\mathcal{M}'' = \overline{\mathcal{M}}\). Este resultado clasifica las **Álgebras de von Neumann** en factores de Tipo I, Tipo II y Tipo III, proporcionando el marco matemático para campos cuánticos continuos, gravedad cuántica y criptografía en espacios de dimensión infinita.
Finalmente, von Neumann abordó la paradoja de la medición identificando la arbitrariedad del **'Corte de Heisenberg'** (*Heisenberg Cut*): la frontera conceptual que separa el sistema observado (cuántico) del observador (clásico). Von Neumann demostró de manera célebre que la ubicación del corte es móvil y no altera las predicciones de medición probabilísticas para un único observador, un principio reevaluado en 2025 para resolver paradojas de observadores múltiples (como la paradoja del amigo de Wigner en cosmología y agujeros negros).
SECCIÓN 2: LA AMENAZA CUÁNTICA CRIPTOGRÁFICA: ANÁLISIS DE ALGORITMOS DE ATAQUE Y VULNERABILIDADES EN BLOCKCHAIN
La seguridad de las redes blockchain clásicas como Bitcoin, Ethereum y Monero descansa sobre dos pilares criptográficos: la **criptografía de clave pública** (utilizada para la generación de direcciones y firmas digitales de transacciones) y las **funciones de hash criptográficas** (utilizadas para el enlace inmutable de bloques, árboles de Merkle y mecanismos de consenso de Prueba de Trabajo). La llegada de ordenadores cuánticos universales destruye las garantías de seguridad de estos cimientos a través de dos algoritmos cuánticos específicos.

TRATADO TÉCNICO:
ARQUITECTURA BLOCKCHAIN, SEGURIDAD POST-CUÁNTICA Y CRIPTOGRAFÍA AVANZADA
Análisis Matemático Exhaustivo de los Algoritmos de Shor y Grover, Protocolos Inter-cadena QLink, Estructuras MTTBA, Escalabilidad Bitcoin L2 (2026), Tokenización RWA y Auditoría IA con GiAnt Corpus
Documento: Informe Técnico de Infraestructura Criptográfica e Interoperabilidad (v2.0)
Fecha de Edición: 21 de Octubre de 2026
Audiencia Objetivo: Arquitectos de Software, Criptógrafos, Ingenieros Web3 y Oficiales de Seguridad
Clasificación: Documento Técnico Corporativo de Alta Precisión

Índice de Contenidos

(El índice de contenidos se actualizará automáticamente al abrir el documento en Microsoft Word o Google Docs).
Resumen Ejecutivo
La convergencia acelerada entre la computación cuántica, la inteligencia artificial y las redes financieras distribuidas exige una reestructuración profunda de la infraestructura criptográfica global. Las arquitecturas de contabilidad distribuida (blockchain) actuales dependen críticamente de esquemas de clave pública como ECDSA (secp256k1 en Bitcoin y Ethereum) y funciones de hash no estructuradas como SHA-256. La llegada inminente de procesadores cuánticos tolerantes a fallos amenaza con invalidar estos cimientos criptográficos mediante algoritmos cuánticos especializados.
■ HALLAZGOS TÉCNICOS Y ESTRATÉGICOS CLAVE
1. Amenaza Cuántica Directa: El algoritmo de Shor reduce la complejidad de romper firmas ECDSA de años en supercomputadores clásicos a un tiempo polinomial O(n³), permitiendo derivar claves privadas a partir de claves públicas expuestas.
2. Degradación del Hash Criptográfico: El algoritmo de Grover acelera la búsqueda en funciones de hash SHA-256 de O(N) a O(√N), reduciendo la seguridad efectiva de 256 bits a 128 bits de entropía.
3. Mitigación Multicapa: La respuesta estructural requiere la transición a Criptografía Post-Cuántica (PQC basada en reticulados como Dilithium/Falcon) e infraestructuras híbridas con Distribución de Claves Cuánticas (QKD) y Módulos de Seguridad de Hardware (HSM) como QLink.
4. Optimización de Capa 1 y L2: La verificación en cadena se optimiza mediante estructuras como MTTBA (reduciendo consumo de energía a 240 Joules y latencia a <100 ms) mientras el ecosistema L2 de Bitcoin (Spark, Stacks, Liquid, Ark) proporciona capacidad transaccional masiva.
5. Auditoría Automatizada con IA: El marco GiAnt y el Corpus de 7,711 vulnerabilidades permiten a los LLMs detectar fallos lógicos en contratos inteligentes con una precisión de juicio humano (4.76/5).

Sección 1: Fundamentos Matemáticos y Físicos de la Mecánica Cuántica (von Neumann)
Las bases matemáticas de la información cuántica moderna se remontan a los trabajos seminales de John von Neumann formulados desde 1927 y reevaluados ampliamente en la física de 2025. Von Neumann unificó las formulaciones de la mecánica matricial de Heisenberg y la mecánica ondulatoria de Schrödinger estableciendo como marco riguroso el espacio de Hilbert complejo H. En esta formulación, los estados puros de un sistema físico se representan como vectores unitarios de estado |ψ⟩ en el espacio de Hilbert, mientras que los observables físicos corresponden a operadores hermíticos auto-adjuntos A = A†.
Para describir ensembled de estados y sistemas cuánticos abiertos caracterizados por incertidumbre estadística, von Neumann introdujo el operador o matriz de densidad ρ. Un estado mixto se expresa formalmente como:
[MATRIZ DE DENSIDAD DE VON NEUMANN]
ρ = ∑_i p_i |ψ_i⟩⟨ψ_i|, donde p_i ≥ 0 y ∑_i p_i = 1
Donde: p_i es la probabilidad estadística del estado puro |ψ_i⟩. La matriz de densidad cumple Tr(ρ) = 1 y ρ ≥ 0.

A partir de la matriz de densidad, von Neumann definió la entropía cuántica para cuantificar la falta de información o el grado de mezcla de un estado físico:
[ENTROPÍA DE VON NEUMANN]
S(ρ) = -Tr(ρ ln ρ) = -∑_i λ_i ln λ_i
Donde: λ_i representan los autovalores del operador de densidad ρ. Para un estado puro, S(ρ) = 0, mientras que para un estado completamente mezclado en dimensión d, S(ρ) = ln(d).

En la teoría de la medición cuántica, von Neumann distinguió entre dos procesos fundamentales de evolución física:
• Proceso 1 (Discontinuo/Irreversible): La medición de un observable A con autovalores a_i y proyectores P_i. El estado colapsa proyectivamente a P_i|ψ⟩ / ||P_i|ψ⟩|| con probabilidad Pr(a_i) = ⟨ψ|P_i|ψ⟩ = Tr(P_i ρ).
• Proceso 2 (Continuo/Reversible): La evolución temporal unitaria gobernada por la ecuación de Schrödinger, |ψ(t)⟩ = U(t)|ψ(0)⟩, donde U(t) = exp(-iHt/ℏ).

Las investigaciones modernas extienden las mediciones proyectivas tradicionales al marco de Medidas de Valores de Operadores Positivos (POVM), definidas por un conjunto de operadores hermíticos {E_i} tales que E_i ≥ 0 y ∑_i E_i = I. Las POVM permiten modelar la extracción óptima de información en presencia de ruido, optimizando la detección en protocolos de comunicación cuántica y criptografía de distribución de claves (QKD).
Sección 2: Ejecución Completa Paso a Paso de Algoritmos Cuánticos contra Criptografía Clásica
2.1 El Algoritmo de Shor: Colapso de Firma Digital (ECDSA y RSA)
El algoritmo de Shor (propuesto por Peter Shor en 1994) resuelve el problema de factorización de enteros y el problema del logaritmo discreto cuántico en tiempo polinomial O(n³), comparado con el algoritmo clásico subexponencial más eficiente (General Number Field Sieve - GNFS). En el contexto de blockchain, la firma digital secp256k1 se basa en el Problema del Logarithmo Discreto de Curva Elíptica (ECDLP): dada la curva y² = x³ + 7 mod p, hallar k escalar tal que P = k · G.
Ejecución Paso a Paso del Algoritmo de Shor desde Cero:

Paso 1: Reducción al Problema del Orden Modular
Hallar el factor de N equivale a determinar el periodo r de la función modular f(x) = a^x mod N para un a entero aleatorio coprimo con N (gcd(a,N)=1). El periodo es el menor entero positivo r tal que:

[REDUCCIÓN MATEMÁTICA DE SHOR]
a^r ≡ 1 (mod N) ⇒ (a^(r/2) - 1)(a^(r/2) + 1) ≡ 0 (mod N)
Donde: Si r es par y a^(r/2) ≢ -1 (mod N), entonces gcd(a^(r/2) ± 1, N) da un factor no trivial de N.

Paso 2: Inicialización del Registro Cuántico
Se emplean dos registros cuánticos. El primer registro contiene m qubits en superposición uniforme (donde Q = 2^m tal que N² ≤ Q < 2N²). El segundo registro contiene n qubits inicializados en |0⟩:

[ESTADO INICIAL DE SHOR]
|ψ_0⟩ = (1 / √Q) ∑_{x=0}^{Q-1} |x⟩ |0⟩
Donde: Superposición uniforme de todos los x de 0 a Q-1 en el registro de entrada.

Paso 3: Exponenciación Modular Cuántica
Se aplica el oráculo cuántico de exponenciación modular U_f |x⟩|0⟩ = |x⟩|a^x mod N⟩, entrelazando ambos registros:

[EVALUACIÓN ORACULAR MODULAR]
|ψ_1⟩ = (1 / √Q) ∑_{x=0}^{Q-1} |x⟩ |a^x mod N⟩
Donde: El valor modular a^x mod N queda grabado en el segundo registro cuántico.

Paso 4: Medición del Segundo Registro y Colapso Periódico
Al medir el segundo registro se obtiene un valor k = a^x0 mod N. El primer registro colapsa a una superposición periódica de estados separados por el periodo r:

[COLAPSO DEL REGISTRO A SUPERPOSICIÓN PERIÓDICA]
|ψ_2⟩ = (1 / √K) ∑_{j=0}^{K-1} |x_0 + j·r⟩
Donde: Donde K ≈ Q/r es el número de repeticiones del periodo dentro del rango Q.

Paso 5: Transformada de Fourier Cuántica (QFT)
Para extraer el periodo r oculto, se aplica la Transformada de Fourier Cuántica sobre el primer registro. La QFT transforma los desplazamientos periódicos en interferencia constructiva en picos de frecuencia y = s·Q/r:

[TRANSFORMADA DE FOURIER CUÁNTICA (QFT)]
QFT |x⟩ = (1 / √Q) ∑_{y=0}^{Q-1} exp(2πi x y / Q) |y⟩
Donde: La medición de y produce un valor cercano a s·Q / r para un entero aleatorio s (0 ≤ s < r).

Paso 6: Algoritmo de Fracciones Continuas y Extracción de Factores
Mediante el algoritmo de fracciones continuas clásico sobre la fracción observada y/Q, se obtiene el valor exacto de r. Finalmente, se calculan los factores primos usando el Algoritmo de Euclides: gcd(a^(r/2) - 1, N) y gcd(a^(r/2) + 1, N).

INFORME TÉCNICO CORPORATIVO NESGESFinance Ecosystem.
Análisis Técnico: Blockchain, Escalabilidad, Tokenización y Criptografía Post-Cuántica
Análisis Integral del Panorama Tecnológico, Auditoría con IA y Seguridad Frente a la Amenaza Cuántica

Fecha de Emisión: Octubre 2026 Origen: Gemini Notebook Studio / NESGESFinance
Clasificación: Documento de Investigación Corporativa Fuentes Analizadas: 10 Fuentes Académicas e Industriales

1. Resumen Ejecutivo
El presente documento técnico proporciona una síntesis rigurosa y exhaustiva de diez investigaciones fundamentales que marcan la vanguardia en tecnología blockchain, sistemas distribuidos, activos del mundo real (RWA), cumplimiento regulatorio, auditoría automatizada mediante inteligencia artificial y resistencia criptográfica frente a la computación cuántica. A través de una perspectiva multidimensional, el análisis conecta las raíces históricas de la criptografía peer-to-peer con las soluciones de infraestructura más avanzadas proyectadas hacia la segunda mitad de esta década.
CONCLUSIÓN ESTRATÉGICA PRINCIPAL
La tecnología blockchain evoluciona desde redes aisladas de baja velocidad hacia un ecosistema distribuido, altamente escalable e interoperable. Sin embargo, esta expansión exige dos pilares críticos: la automatización rigurosa de la auditoría de contratos inteligentes respaldada por inteligencia artificial y una transición proactiva hacia la criptografía post-cuántica (PQC) y mecanismos de capa 3 con distribución de claves cuánticas (QKD) antes de la maduración de los ordenadores cuánticos.

Los hallazgos clave identificados a lo largo del corpus documental se estructuran en cinco pilares de innovación:
• Orígenes y Eficiencia Estructural: Desde la formulación original de Bitcoin por Satoshi Nakamoto, la optimización de estructuras de datos como MTTBA demuestra que es posible reducir sustancialmente los nodos redundantes del árbol de Merkle, logrando tiempos de autenticación inferiores a 100 milisegundos con un consumo de solo 240 julios.
• Escalabilidad Multicapa en Bitcoin: El ecosistema de Capa 2 de Bitcoin se diversifica en seis arquitecturas principales (Lightning, Liquid, Rootstock, Stacks, Spark y Ark), complementadas por capacidades de emisión nativa mediante Ordinals, BRC-20 y el protocolo Runes.
• Tokenización RWA y Rigor Regulatorio: La digitalización de activos físicos marcha en paralelo con marcos legales estrictos como la ley GENIUS Act de 2025 en EE. UU., exigiendo la integración automatizada de controles KYC, AML, filtrado OFAC y la regla de viaje (Travel Rule) directamente en la infraestructura de billeteras empresariales.
• Auditoría de Contratos con IA (GiAnt): La auditoría automatizada alcanza un nivel experto gracias al corpus GiAnt, que destila 7,711 hallazgos de vulnerabilidades de Code4rena mediante razonamiento en cadena de pensamiento (Chain-of-Thought) y validación lógica con LLMs.
• Resistencia Cuántica e Interoperabilidad (QLink): Frente al riesgo inminente de los algoritmos de Shor y Grover, se desarrollan arquitecturas de puente de Capa 3 como QLink, que combinan canales QKD, firmas post-cuánticas (Dilithium/Falcon) y módulos HSM para garantizar transferencias entre cadenas inmunes a interceptaciones cuánticas.
2. Fundamentos de Bitcoin y Autenticación Criptográfica Eficiente
2.1 La Visión Original de Satoshi Nakamoto (Satoshi Nakamoto - AWS)
La compilación documental de las comunicaciones de Satoshi Nakamoto entre 2008 y 2010 ('The Book of Satoshi') consolida los fundamentos teóricos y operacionales que dieron origen a la primera moneda digital descentralizada. Nakamoto resolvió el dilema histórico del doble gasto sin recurrir a intermediarios de confianza mediante la integración de una red peer-to-peer y un sello de tiempo distribuido basado en prueba de trabajo (Proof-of-Work) derivado de Hashcash.
El sistema establece una cadena inmutable de bloques en la que las transacciones se aseguran mediante funciones de hash criptográfico (SHA-256) y firmas digitales de clave pública/privada (ECDSA secp256k1). Nakamoto anticipó aspectos operacionales clave como el ajuste dinámico de la dificultad de minado cada 2,016 bloques (aproximadamente dos semanas), la simulación de clientes ligeros mediante verificación simplificada de pagos (SPV) y la transición gradual del modelo de incentivos desde subsidios por bloque hacia un mercado autosostenible de tarifas.
2.2 Autenticación Eficiente mediante MTTBA (Gracy & Jeyavadhanam)
A pesar de la elegancia del protocolo original, las estructuras de datos tradicionales presentan ineficiencias computacionales bajo altas cargas de transacciones. El estudio de Gracy & Jeyavadhanam aborda la duplicación innecesaria de nodos en los árboles de Merkle convencionales cuando un bloque contiene un número impar de transacciones.
La solución propuesta, denominada Autenticación Blockchain basada en Árboles Recortados de Merkle (MTTBA), elimina la duplicación al emparejar el nodo impar sobrante directamente con el nodo inicial del árbol. Esta modificación estructural reduce el número total de nodos requeridos a la fórmula matemática t_n = 2n - 1, optimizando de manera drástica el uso de memoria y la velocidad de hashing.
A continuación se comparan las métricas operativas obtenidas experimentalmente por el protocolo MTTBA frente a la arquitectura clásica de Merkle:
Métrica de Rendimiento Árbol de Merkle Tradicional Protocolo MTTBA
Estructura de Nodos Sobrantes Duplicación del último nodo impar Emparejamiento con el primer nodo
Tiempo de Autenticación > 350 milisegundos < 100 milisegundos
Consumo Energético por Bloque Elevado (> 600 Joules) Reducido a 240 Joules
Consumo de Memoria RAM Aprox. 320 MB - 450 MB Optimizado a 140 MB (99.30% seguridad)

3. Escalabilidad de Capa 2 y Nuevos Estándares en Bitcoin
3.1 Panorama del Ecosistema de Capa 2 en 2026 (Spark)
Debido a que la Capa 1 de Bitcoin limita deliberadamente su rendimiento a 3-7 transacciones por segundo (TPS) para priorizar la descentralización y la seguridad extrema, la expansión del ecosistema requiere soluciones externas de procesamiento off-chain. El informe de investigación de Spark (2026) presenta una clasificación taxonómica completa de las seis arquitecturas dominantes de Capa 2 (L2):
• Canales de Estado (Lightning Network): Utilizan contratos de compromiso firmados off-chain mediante canales 2-de-2 y contratos HTLC, ofreciendo transacciones instantáneas con tarifas insignificantes.
• Cadenas Laterales Federadas (Liquid Network): Administradas por una federación funcional de 60 miembros con custodia multisig 11-de-15, habilitando activos confidenciales y transferencias rápidas de B-BTC.
• Cadenas Laterales de Minería Combinada (Rootstock / RSK): Aseguradas por más del 81% del hash rate global de Bitcoin mediante merge-mining, proporcionando ejecución de contratos inteligentes totalmente compatibles con la EVM de Ethereum.
• Cadenas de Prueba de Transferencia (Stacks): Actualizadas mediante la mejora 'Nakamoto', reduciendo el tiempo de bloque a 5 segundos e introduciendo sBTC como un peg bidireccional descentralizado.
• Cadenas de Estado / Statechains (Spark): Implementan arquitecturas en hoja apoyadas en firmas umbral FROST de 2-de-2 y un modelo de seguridad 1-de-n, permitiendo transferencias de propiedad de UTXO sin la gestión compleja de canales.
• Protocolos UTXO Virtuales / VTXO (Ark): Mecanismo descentralizado basado en rondas de lotes fuera de la cadena con fechas de expiración absoluta, previniendo el almacenamiento masivo en la cadena principal.
Asimismo, el informe destaca el impacto inminente de propuestas de bifurcación blanda para convenios (covenants, como BIP 119 CTV) y la verificación optimista programable mediante BitVM, la cual permite computación Turing-completa en Bitcoin sin alterar su capa de consenso.
